newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH RAIL ENGINE DRIVERS GIVE UP PLANNED STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH RAIL ENGINE DRIVERS GIVE UP PLANNED STRIKE.

text.p: Poland's train drivers' trade union dropped its plans for an indefinite pay strike after it signed an agreement late on Thursday with the board of Polish State Railways (PKP), PKP's spokeswoman said.

"Late on Thursday the Board of PKP signed an agreement with the rail engine drivers' trade union and the union decided to give up the strike which was to start on Saturday," Anna Raczkowska said in a statement.
The union wanted the PKP management to keep real wages at the current levels and to increase employment.

"The new labour law, which came into effect on January 1, envisages working time and organisation changes which would decrease rail engine drivers' wages," Andrzej Krawczyk, head of PKP's social and employee department told Reuters.
"Therefore, we have agreed to compensate this group in other ways," he said.
Krawczyk added that the PKP board would meet with all unions operating in the company on January 31 and set the ceiling for wage growth in the firm in 1997.
"The board's proposal is to adopt the same ceiling as the one negotiatied in the trilateral committee of the government, trade unions and employers," he said.
The trilateral committee, which met in August 1996, agreed that wages in the state-owned enterprise sector would grow 17 percent this year against average annual inflation seen at 15 percent.
